questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-conservative force?
questions.explanation: Work done by friction depends on the path taken and cannot be recovered, so no potential energy can be defined for it. The other three are conservative.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The root mean square value of an alternating current of peak value I₀ is:
questions.explanation: I(rms) = I₀/√2, about 0.707 I₀, and it is this value that ammeters read and that produces the same heating as an equal steady current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Maxwell introduced the idea of displacement current to account for the fact that a changing electric field also:
options: Has no effect outside a conductor
questions.explanation: Without it Ampere's law fails in the gap of a charging capacitor. The symmetry of changing fields producing each other is what allows electromagnetic waves to travel through vacuum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A sigma bond is stronger than a pi bond because in a sigma bond the orbitals overlap:
options: Along the internuclear axis, giving greater overlap
questions.explanation: End-on overlap concentrates electron density between the nuclei, while a pi bond's sideways overlap is weaker, which is why pi bonds break first in addition reactions.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The average oxidation number of carbon in glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is:
questions.explanation: Taking H as +1 and O as -2: 6x + 12(+1) + 6(-2) = 0, so 6x = 0 and x = 0. An average oxidation number can also be fractional.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: An optically active alkyl halide undergoing an SN1 reaction gives a nearly racemic product because:
options: The intermediate carbocation is planar and can be attacked from either face
The nucleophile attacks from the back only
The product has no chiral carbon
No bond is broken in the reaction
questions.explanation: Attack on the two faces of the flat carbocation is almost equally likely, so both enantiomers form. SN2 instead gives inversion of configuration because attack is strictly from the back.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 6: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The stacks of thylakoids inside a chloroplast are called:
questions.explanation: Grana hold the photosynthetic pigments and carry out the light reaction, while the surrounding stroma contains the enzymes of the Calvin cycle.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The phosphorus cycle differs from the nitrogen and carbon cycles in that phosphorus:
options: Has a large gaseous reservoir in the atmosphere
Is a sedimentary cycle with rock as its main reservoir and no significant gaseous phase
Is not needed by living organisms
questions.explanation: Weathering of rock releases phosphate, which is why phosphorus often limits productivity, and once washed into deep sediments it returns only over geological time.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in a healthy human adult is about:
options: 125 mL per minute, that is about 180 litres per day
questions.explanation: Nearly 180 litres is filtered daily but only about 1.5 litres leaves as urine, since over 99 percent of the filtrate is reabsorbed by the tubules.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 16: Excretory Products and their Elimination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A single gene affecting several apparently unrelated traits, as in phenylketonuria, is an example of:
questions.explanation: One defective enzyme leads to mental retardation along with reduced hair and skin pigmentation. Polygenic inheritance is the opposite case, many genes shaping one trait.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
